item.title: Venus and Serena Williams' highly anticipated US Open return ends in heartbreaking loss
item.description: Venus and Serena Williams returned to Arthur Ashe Stadium for a thrilling three-set US Open doubles match that kept fans on the edge of their seats.
item.content:encoded:
For the first time in four years, Venus and Serena Williams returned to the US Open court together Friday night in Queens.

The legendary sisters were set to reunite earlier this summer at Wimbledon; however, Serena — who, at 44, is in the midst of a comeback after several years away from the sport — was forced to withdraw due to injury.

Friday night, the two walked onto the court at Arthur Ashe Stadium to a massive ovation from the crowd.

GROUP OF INFLUENCERS FORCES PAUSE DURING US OPEN MATCH WITH CRINGEWORTHY PHOTOSHOOT IN SUITE

Serena's jacket listed her US Open titles, including the pair of doubles titles that she and Venus won in 1999 and 2009.

Their opponents were Taiwan’s Chan Hao-ching and Australian Maya Joint, who, at 20 years old, was just a toddler when the Williams sisters won the 2009 US Open.

The first set was fairly back and forth to start, but Chan and Joint pulled ahead to win it 6-3.

The Williams sisters responded and started the second set strong, but it went the distance, needing a seven-point tie-breaker to decide the winner.

In the tie-breaker, Venus and Serena had multiple opportunities to put Chan and Joint away, but they fought back. Finally, after the scare, the Williamses clinched the set to keep the match going.

While they were respectful throughout the match, there was no question that the overwhelming majority of the crowd was behind the sisters, erupting after every point.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The tennis greats battled back against an impressive pairing that is only in their fourth event together to force a decisive tie-breaker in the final set.

The Williamses took the first five points in a row to jump out to an early lead; however, Joint and Chan took the next three.

Joint and Chan battled back to take the lead, and in the end, they walked away with the win in the match that was just a shade over three hours.

In the end, it was a fantastic three-set thriller, 6–3, 6–7(6), 7–6(10), that showed the Williams sisters — already all-time greats of the sport — are still a force to be reckoned with.

item.title: From cockroach milk to stepping on snakes, Ig Nobel awards celebrates science at its oddest
item.description: Cockroach milk, kissing evolution and the underwear soil test were among the unusual real studies honored at the Ig Nobel ceremony in Zurich.
item.content:encoded:
A motley crew of scientists was honored this week for its unusual contributions, which included studying cockroach milk, the evolutionary history of kissing and testing soil health by using underwear.

The satirical Ig Nobel ceremony, which honors unusual but real studies, took place in Zurich Thursday and was presented by the digital magazine, the Annals of Improbable Research.

The awards, which were founded in 1991, took place outside the U.S. for the first time this year over the concern that the honorees wouldn’t be able to get a visa.

Other winners included researchers who found upper-class people were more likely to engage in unethical behavior, such as stealing candy from a baby, a study on proper nose blowing and gently stepping on snakes to see what provokes them into biting people.

WASHINGTON HOMEOWNER HEARS MYSTERIOUS BANGING CALLS 911 BEFORE POLICE FIND GROWLING BOBCAT AT TOP OF STAIRS

"The general pattern seems to be that, with wealth and rising power, you become less engaged with the needs of others and less burdened by the needs of social relationships," Dr. Paul Piff, a social psychologist at the University of California, Irvine said, according to the Guardian. 

"Taking candy from children might be the least of our worries, but it’s emblematic of the tendency to prioritize one’s own needs over those of others."

The final four honorees included those studying the power of having mutual enemies, attempts at a splash-free urinal, using dead mosquitos for 3D printing and research that found parents love the smell of their newborn babies but not teenage children.

In case you’re wondering, the team studying the history of kissing has defined it as "a non-agonistic interaction involving directed, intraspecific, oral-oral contact with some movement of the lips/mouthparts and no food transfer." Romantic.

COUPLE PUBLICLY CANED AFTER ALLEGED TIKTOK KISS SPARKS OUTRAGE IN INDONESIA

"Next time you kiss someone, you can think, 'This is a 21.5 million-year-old tradition that I'm honoring here," evolutionary biologist Matilda Brindle of the University of Oxford said, according to NPR. "It's not just a modern human behavior. It's really ancestral.' And to us, that suggests that it probably has quite a useful evolutionary function."

Brindle said her team believes that Neanderthals not only kissed each other. They may have also kissed early humans.

CAVE DISCOVERY PUSHES BACK EVIDENCE OF HUMAN ANCESTORS USING FIRE TO 1.79M YEARS AGO

All the honorees receive a trophy that looks like a cross between a mushroom and a human foot while the audience throws paper airplanes at them.

The Ig Nobel has no relation to the actual Nobel Prize, which will announce its honorees in October.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: DOJ ordered to freeze antitrust work with Canada as trade tensions intensify
item.description: The Justice Department's antitrust division was directed to pause all cooperation with Canada amid the escalating U.S.-Canada trade war, according to a report.
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Justice Department's antitrust division was directed earlier this week to pause all work with the Canadian government as the trade dispute between the neighboring nations intensifies, according to a report.

The chief of the antitrust division's international section, Lynda Marshall, ordered officials on Wednesday to halt all cooperation on cases and engagement on policy issues with Canadian authorities, without providing a reason for the directive, according to emails obtained by The Wall Street Journal.

Section chiefs in the antitrust division were also instructed in another email on Friday to provide lists outlining areas of cooperation with Canada by the end of the day, according to the newspaper.

NEW YORK GOV HOCHUL REJECTS TRUMP'S 'LAKE AMERICA' RENAMING WITH BLUNT MESSAGE

The DOJ disputed the report, saying in a statement that the "alleged direction was never given to anyone."

The division was asked to "temporarily hold off on a scheduled meeting on a specific investigation until the DOJ's antitrust team had more time to prepare," the department said.

This comes as the U.S. and Canada, which have been close allies for decades, continue to spar over President Donald Trump's trade war against Ottawa and subsequent targeting of the U.S.'s northern neighbor, which most recently included the president's executive order to rename Lake Ontario to "Lake America."

Although the renaming only applies to the U.S. federal government, while Canada, other international bodies and U.S. states are not forced to follow the rebranding, the order adds to the ongoing tensions between the two countries that arose following Trump's return to the White House in January 2025.

The trade war has led to tariffs on tens of billions of dollars in cross-border trade.

TRUMP RENAMES LAKE ONTARIO 'LAKE AMERICA' AMID INTENSIFYING US-CANADA TRADE DISPUTE

The Canadian government said it would impose retaliatory tariffs on the U.S. beginning Sept. 8 in response to the Trump administration’s new 50% tariffs on about $20 billion worth of Canadian goods, which took effect last month.

Prime Minister Mark Carney said Canada "will match Washington's new tariffs dollar for dollar in order to protect Canadian workers, farmers, families, and businesses."

The Wall Street Journal and Reuters contributed to this report.

item.title: TCU does an about-face after stripping local newspaper's credentials days before football season
item.description: TCU Athletics restored press credentials to the Fort Worth Star-Telegram days after pulling them over a report about Jacob Fields' dismissal.
item.content:encoded:
Texas Christian University has changed its position and decided to reinstate press credentials for the Fort Worth Star-Telegram after pulling them last week, just days before the team got their season underway.

The Horned Frogs' season opener was across the pond in Dublin, Ireland, where they took on the Bill Belichick-led University of North Carolina Tar Heels, but Star-Telegram TCU reporter Steven Johnson had to cover the game from the stands.

That was because, as OutKick's Ian Miller wrote, the university had pulled the outlet's credentials because of a report about a locker room altercation that resulted in the dismissal of senior safety Jacob Fields.

FORMER TCU SAFETY JACOB FIELDS CHARGED WITH AGGRAVATED ASSAULT AFTER ALLEGED LOCKER ROOM INCIDENT

Ironically, the Horned Frogs play their games at Amon G. Carter Stadium, which is named after the Fort Worth Star-Telegram's founder and publisher.

However, the school has changed its tune and is reinstating the paper.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"Today, TCU Athletics fully restored media credentials to the Fort Worth Star-Telegram," the athletic department's statement reads. "In a series of productive discussions, we made clear our position and resolved to move forward. We respect their role as an independent news source and voice in our community, and we look forward to the season ahead."

So, it sounds like the hatchet has been buried.

TCU lost that game against UNC in Ireland by a score of 15-10.

item.title: Migrants spark outrage after video shows baby dolphin beaten during beach celebration
item.description: Video from Ceuta shows migrants pulling a dolphin calf from the water and striking it with a stick as outraged residents tried to intervene on the beach.
item.content:encoded:
Migrants in the North African Spanish enclave of Ceuta were captured on video hitting a young dolphin and possibly killing it while celebrating.

Video circulating online shows a group of men and boys triumphantly lifting what appeared to be a baby bottlenose dolphin calf above their heads as onlookers gleefully cheered. 

The dolphin swam too close to shore when a group of men allegedly pulled it from El Trampolin beach.

The celebration appeared to enrage local residents, who tried to stop the group's actions during a confrontation.

ONE OF WORLD’S OLDEST ORCA WHALES FOUND WITH POSSIBLE SHOTGUN WOUNDS AS OFFICIALS LAUNCH INVESTIGATION

One of the men reportedly struck the dolphin with a stick, mortally wounding it. Some people were heard shouting "no" in the video, and some men were cheering. Others appeared concerned at the treatment of the marine mammal.

Someone eventually took the mammal and placed it back in the water. The incident has sparked outrage among Ceuta residents.

BOATER'S STUNT TO AWAKEN SLEEPING POLAR BEAR BACKFIRES AFTER BRAZEN HORN BLAST

"On Wednesday, September 2, 2026, a disoriented dolphin calf swimming near the shore at Trampolin Beach, in Ceuta, was brutally pulled from the water," Nadia Garcia Gomez wrote in a social media post announcing a petition to have those involved arrested. 

"Eyewitnesses and local media reported that the animal was handled as if it were an object and violently struck on the head with a stick, causing its immediate death."

Gomez called the migrants' actions an act of "extreme and unjustifiable cruelty" that cannot go unpunished. She noted that dolphins are a protected species under Spanish and European laws.

LOCALS TORCH MIGRANT SHELTERS AS SPAIN'S PM POINTS BLAME BEYOND THE BORDER

Other Ceuta residents have called for the migrants involved to be prosecuted and expelled from the country.

Ceuta has been gripped by an influx of migrants from neighboring Morocco. In July, more than 70,000 migrants stormed the tiny enclave's border defenses. Although most of the migrants returned home shortly afterward, thousands have remained.

TENS OF THOUSANDS FLOOD STREETS TO PROTEST SPAIN BORDER CRISIS

Some residents have called for deportations and tougher action from the central government in Madrid. Last week, angry locals tore down migrant tents and shelters at the beach.

item.title: Politician Spencer Pratt calls out actor Ryan Reynolds for condemning 1980s nostalgia
item.description: Spencer Pratt fires back at Ryan Reynolds over his "Mayday" premiere comments, contrasting the anti-hero generation with classic 1980s cinema heroes.
item.content:encoded:
Former reality TV star and California politician Spencer Pratt offered a blistering response Friday after actor Ryan Reynolds condemned nostalgia for the 1980s.

Ryan Reynolds had initially faced backlash Thursday after the "Deadpool" star called the 1980s "brutal" and a "f---ing mess" while promoting his Cold War-era movie "Mayday" at its New York premiere, prompting critics to question his characterization of the decade and the contrast with his nostalgia-driven new film.

"When you get far enough away from a time period that’s quite distinct, there’s always a lovely feeling associated with it, almost like you pave over all the trauma with puppy dogs and ice cream," Reynolds said in an interview with Variety. 

RYAN REYNOLDS STARS AS SHOT-DOWN NAVY PILOT RESCUED BY EX-KGB AGENT IN APPLE TV+’S ‘MAYDAY’

"The '80s was a brutal, brutal time for people. It was a f---ing mess, and people forget that."

Pratt, however, argued that the 1980s were a time of cultural sanity compared to today’s world, one where there were clearly defined ideals of good and evil.

"It makes perfect sense that Ryan Reynolds' view of the 80s is the inverse of what normal people think. In 80s movies, bad guys were villains. Today, the bad guys are the heroes. Hollywood now bends over backwards to redeem wickedness and mental illness," he said on X. 

"'Top Gun' and St Thomas of Cruise represent the hero generation of cinema. Reynolds represents the anti-hero generation, and they are both byproducts of their own creations. Choose your path carefully, young man."

Reynolds, in recent years, has played the Marvel superhero/anti-hero Deadpool, who is a wisecracking mercenary who breaks the fourth wall of the Marvel Universe and stands as a stark contrast against the more traditional superhero archetype.

Pratt shared his tweet with an excerpt from a video he had previously shared in which he was talking about far-left politics among women and the "hijacking of the maternal instinct" and the loss of classic heroes as American culture began to try to empathize with anti-heroes or even outright villains.

Christian Toto, an award-winning film critic and founder of Hollywood in Toto, spoke to Fox News Digital about how Pratt’s response to Reynolds points to a very real fissure in American culture.

"Spencer Pratt's hot take suggests a sobering reality. Has pop culture's infatuation with anti-heroes had real-world implications? It's one thing to follow Tony Soprano or Walter White, but modern films and TV shows are replete with villains we're asked to cheer on," he said. 

"Consider how many recent movies have given us hit men with hearts of gold. ‘Bullet Train.’ ‘Hit Man.’ The ‘John Wick’ saga. Indie films like ‘Emily the Criminal’ and ‘Carolina Caroline’ also turn villains into quasi-heroes.

SPENCER PRATT'S LA MAYORAL CAMPAIGN VIDEO DRAWS JOHN WICK COMPARISONS AS FANS RALLY BEHIND HIM

"Has that had a corrosive effect on the culture? Pratt's question is worth exploring.

"His takedown of Reynolds' comments also leave[s] a mark. No decade is perfect. The '80s gave us the AIDS crisis, worries about nuclear war, the Challenger explosion and more. It also delivered great pop culture classics and lacked the cultural hand-wringing that weighs down so much of our lives today. It was a more simple time, and it's impossible not to miss that," he concluded.

Theo Wold, former assistant attorney general and former White House deputy assistant for domestic policy under President Donald Trump, offered a more explicitly political angle.

"Ryan Reynolds forgot to do some thinking before he took a talking point from his celebrity cocktail hours and debuted it in public. Most of us remember the '80s, and it was a time when this country enjoyed greater social cohesion and wider individual freedoms than today, with relative economic prosperity," he said. 

"Of course, Reynolds’ experience growing up in Canada might have been different — socialism was working just as poorly then as it is now.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

"Also, only a vapid Hollywood celebrity would cite the 'Cuban Missile Crisis' as an explanation for why the 1980s were supposedly so 'brutal,' rather than, say, the horrific crimes perpetrated by radical leftists like domestic terrorists Angela Davis and Bill Ayers."

item.title: Move over, South Beach: 3 quiet Florida beach alternatives to try this Labor Day weekend
item.description: Skip South Beach, Clearwater Beach, and Daytona Beach this Labor Day weekend and try three hidden Florida beaches that locals have sworn by.
item.content:encoded:
With Labor Day weekend approaching like a freight train, that can only mean one thing: summer is unofficially over.

At least, that's what I would be saying if I lived in any of the other lower 48 states not named Florida.

Beach season is measured more by the days you can't go rather than the days you can, and those no-go's are few and far between.

SUMMER TRAVEL PSA: IF YOU COME TO FLORIDA LOOKING FOR GREAT BEACHES, STAY AWAY FROM THE KEYS

Labor Day just so happens to be one of the most popular beach days in the state, as it is in other locales across the country, and this year will be no different.

Folks from all over the world will be enjoying the white sandy shores of the Sunshine State, and that means if you want to partake in some beach action, you might have to go off the beaten path unless you want to rub elbows with the unwashed masses.

AMERICANS CHOOSING TO VISIT SMALLER TOWNS OVER BIG CITIES AS TRAVEL COSTS RISE

Luckily for you, I grew up in Florida and spent my entire life trying to find strips of sand that weren't overrun with fraternity chapters and New Jerseyans - since their beaches apparently will be underwater soon - and now I want to share my findings with you.

Here are three beaches in my home state that you MUST check out as alternatives to some of the more well-known spots.

When you think of beaches in South Florida, there's a good chance your mind immediately jumps to South Beach or perhaps Fort Lauderdale Beach.

Well, odds are both of those places will be overrun with tourists this weekend (and every weekend), so skip those and head to Dania Beach.

Situated just on the other side of Port Everglades, Dania Beach is a quiet strip of land smack dab in between Miami and Fort Lauderdale, and while everyone else is partying it up in those two cities, you'll enjoy the relaxing side of SoFlo living here.

The north end of the beach features Whiskey Creek, a quiet brackish river that is great for kayaking and occasionally spotting some manatees (though highly unlikely at this time of year).

Further south, you will find the Dania Pier, featuring the local restaurant Quarterdeck and plenty of fishing opportunities, so long as you pay a small fee to access the far end of the pier.

The seagrape trees and dunes offer a chance for wildlife lovers to spot plenty of birds along with other creatures that call these beaches home, and the water is exceptionally calm for an Atlantic shore.

ONCE-GLAMOROUS VACATION SPOT OVERRUN BY INFLUENCERS AND CROWDS: 'ALMOST UNBEARABLE'

Dania is a perfect spot to slow things down this Labor Day weekend, so check it out if you're in the area.

The Tampa-St. Pete-Clearwater area is home to some of the most famous beaches in the country, but that also means everyone and their grandmother will be there soaking up this sun this holiday weekend.

Hop in the car and drive an hour south to Lido Key Beach in Sarasota to remedy that.

Sarasota is one of Florida's best kept secrets, and although many locals swear by Siesta Key or Anna Maria Island, Lido Key offers the same pristine white beaches without the pomp and circumstance of the other two.

It's family-friendly, so you won't have to worry about watching Sigma Chi try and funnel a keg of suds in front of your kids, and the views are spectacular; truly some of the best the state has to offer in that regard.

You'll feel like you're staring at a postcard as the sun sets over the Gulf.

For those of you feeling adventurous, there are guided kayak tours that take you through the mangroves, and jet ski rentals are available if you want to get a little wind through your hair.

Make it a Labor Day to remember for all the right reasons and head to Lido Key.

I might get myself in some hot water with my friends and family for revealing this spot, but if you want serenity and tranquility for your beach weekend, this is the place to be.

Daytona Beach has a reputation as being a spring breaker's paradise, and I've never figured out why.

Regardless, the place will be slammed all weekend, so if you're up for a little drive, less than an hour and a half north is Villano Beach.

Just east of downtown St. Augustine, Villano Beach is a small and fairly unknown Atlantic beach that is really only frequented by locals and campers, given that the North Beach Campground sits across Jimmy Buffett Memorial Highway.

The parking lot that leads to the shore only has about 30 spots, but I've never seen all of them taken, and it's one of the few points where you can access the beach, if that gives you an idea of just how untapped this place is.

The sand is abundant and wide open, as Villano Beach offers a ton of runway to set up a tent or giant umbrella and stake your claim for the majority of the day.

This is a no-frills type of beach, so if you just want to relax and hear the crashing of the waves and maybe do a little body surfing, this is your jam.

And, when you've worked up an appetite, stroll into The Reef for some upscale seafood or Aunt Kate's across the street on the intracoastal side for some more laidback eats and a great view of the sunset.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

You can't go wrong with either after a long day in the sun.

item.title: WATCH: Illegal alien busted in battleground state after allegedly committing voter fraud
item.description: Exclusive footage obtained by Fox News shows HSI agents executing arrests as the Trump administration ramps up a nationwide crackdown on non-citizen voting ahead of the 2026 midterms.
item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE: Footage obtained by Fox News Digital shows federal agents executing a sweep linked to a multi-state Department of Justice (DOJ) probe that has resulted in criminal charges against individuals for illegal voting, falsifying citizenship status and other election fraud related charges in Pennsylvania, New Jersey, and Wisconsin.

The charges arrive as part of a highly publicized nationwide surge by the Trump administration to hunt down election-related crimes ahead of the 2026 midterms.

Over the past year, the Justice Department has filed lawsuits against nearly 30 states to force the surrender of confidential voter rolls, while simultaneously repurposing Homeland Security Investigations (HSI)—an agency historically focused on cartels and terrorism—to spearhead a search for unlawfully registered non-citizens.

"Despite the media and Democrats claiming it never happens, the evidence of non-citizens registering to vote in our elections continues to pile up," White House spokesperson Lauren Bis told Fox News Digital. "Any non-citizens found registering to vote and voting in our elections will be held accountable. Only Americans should be electing American leaders."

‘RAW MATERIAL FOR ELECTION FRAUD’: EXPERT FLAGS VOTER-ROLL PROBLEMS FAR BEYOND ONE STATE

The Justice Department announced Friday that five people—including two illegal immigrants and two non-citizens with legal status—had been federally charged with unlawfully casting ballots, falsifying citizenship status, fraudulently registering to vote and aiding and abetting during the 2022 and 2024 elections. 

Some of the arrestees, according to a DOJ press release, could face up to more than a decade in prison if found guilty of providing a false statement of citizenship in order to vote and other election fraud charges they are facing. Fox News Digital obtained footage of the arrest of one of those individuals, Katya Rodriguez, 30.

An illegal alien from Mexico living in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania, Rodriguez was indicted by a federal grand jury on charges related to illegally voting as an alien in the 2024 election. In particular, she is facing allegations of providing a false statement of citizenship to vote, fraudulent registration and voting as an alien, according to a DOJ press release, and could serve a maximum 11 years in prison, a term of supervised release, and be forced to pay a fine.

SPANBERGER FACT-CHECKED AFTER TRUMP MAIL-VOTING WARNING RAISES MILITARY BALLOT FEARS

The Trump administration's federal enforcement action comes just weeks after New Jersey officials disclosed a massive state software error that mistakenly registered nearly 6,600 non-citizens to vote, with roughly 400 casting ballots. 

Meanwhile, Homeland Security announced earlier this summer that an audit of public voter rolls had identified more than 250,000 registered noncitizens in just four states: California, Pennsylvania, New Jersey and Nevada.

Just days ago, internal directives revealed by CNN showed Homeland Security Investigations launching a coordinated "voter fraud surge" into nine key states—including Pennsylvania and Wisconsin—to hunt down non-citizens suspected of election interference. The handful of arrests announced Friday are among the latest enforcement actions.

"Homeland Security Investigations is committed to safeguarding the integrity of our nation’s election systems and ensuring that allegations of unlawful voting, fraudulent registration, and other election-related crimes are thoroughly investigated," said HSI Acting Executive Associate Director John A. Condon. 

"The American people deserve confidence that our elections are protected from fraud and criminal exploitation, and that those who seek to undermine the law are held accountable," he continued. "As reflected in these cases, HSI special agents worked alongside our federal partners to identify alleged criminal conduct, follow the evidence, and support prosecutions that reinforce public trust and uphold the rule of law."

item.title: Cathy Engelbert will be remembered as the commissioner who made the WNBA deeply political and divisive
item.description: WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert announced her retirement after 2026, but her seven-year tenure was defined by player clashes and political controversy.
item.content:encoded:
WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert announced Friday that she would retire following the 2026 season after seven years in the role.

Engelbert took over in 2019 as the WNBA’s first commissioner, and there is no question the league is substantially bigger, more visible and more valuable than when she arrived. The league expanded, secured major media-rights agreements, introduced charter travel and negotiated significant increases in player compensation through a new collective bargaining agreement signed before the 2026 season. NBA Commissioner Adam Silver has called Engelbert’s tenure the most significant period of growth in WNBA history. But does she deserve credit for these successes? I believe the answer is clear.

Being commissioner isn’t simply about revenue, television ratings or franchise valuations. A commissioner must also maintain relationships with the players, and those relationships have been objectively tumultuous throughout Engelbert’s tenure. She must protect the league’s reputation and its stars, an area in which she has also fallen short. She must manage controversies, something she has repeatedly failed to do. Finally, she must ensure the on-court product is entertaining and credible, which is arguably the strongest case in her favor.

It goes without saying that Engelbert’s tenure has become increasingly contentious, helping lead to her decision to retire.

SUE BIRD CLAIMS WNBA PLAYERS WANTED TO 'SHUT UP AND DRIBBLE' DESPITE LEADING 2020 POLITICAL PUSH

Engelbert’s first major test came almost immediately. The COVID-19 pandemic threatened the 2020 season, but the WNBA successfully created the "Wubble" — a play on words combining WNBA and bubble — in Florida and completed the season.

While it was a success that the season was able to be played, the league also embraced an increasingly prominent social-justice role. I truly believe this is where the WNBA became the most politically divisive league in America. Players wore social-justice messages, including support for criminal Jacob Blake and Black Lives Matter, which was led by self-described Marxists, and the league partnered with players on racial-justice initiatives. Engelbert allowed all of this to happen and disenfranchised fans who didn’t care for the overt political messaging when they turned to sports as an escape.

Engelbert also allowed herself and the league to be bullied by radical left-wing activist players who ousted Atlanta Dream owner and Republican Sen. Kelly Loeffler while publicly supporting Raphael Warnock through "Vote Warnock" T-shirts on the court because Loeffler publicly opposed the league’s Black Lives Matter messaging.

When the league could have focused on basketball, Engelbert helped the WNBA become completely intertwined with left-wing politics.

One of the most serious controversies of Engelbert's tenure involved former Las Vegas Aces star Dearica Hamby.

Hamby alleged that she experienced bullying and mistreatment after revealing that she was pregnant. The WNBA investigated the situation and determined that the Aces had violated league rules concerning impermissible benefits during contract negotiations involving Hamby.

The league punished Las Vegas by taking away a first-round draft pick and suspending coach Becky Hammon for two games.

The controversy raised a larger question about how seriously professional sports organizations protect pregnant athletes.

It also placed Engelbert in the uncomfortable position of having to demonstrate that the league's commitment to women's sports extended to protecting players who become mothers.

For years, WNBA teams primarily traveled commercially because charter flights were considered financially impractical under league economics.

That became increasingly controversial as players complained about exhausting travel schedules and safety concerns.

The issue became particularly embarrassing for the league because teams had previously been punished for using unauthorized charter flights.

Then, in 2024, with the influx of attention, security concerns, and money due to Caitlin Clark, Engelbert announced that the WNBA would introduce a league-wide charter program.

Engelbert was right that charter flights didn’t make financial sense before Clark arrived, so I can give her some credit. Ultimately, however, Clark deserves the credit for this, not Engelbert.

CAITLIN CLARK CALLS FOR FULL-TIME WNBA REFEREES AS OFFICIATING FAILURES MOUNT IN 2026

The explosion of Clark's popularity also exposed another problem: the WNBA's handling of physical play and officiating.

Clark was repeatedly involved in controversial physical incidents, and fans increasingly questioned whether the league was protecting its biggest star. The answer? No.

Engelbert was given a gift and she did little to nothing to protect her golden goose.

Players and coaches complained about inconsistent officiating, physicality and a lack of accountability. Engelbert eventually announced a committee focused on the "state of the game" and officiating after concerns escalated.

The level of incompetence from the top down was damning. Without Clark, the WNBA wouldn't reach new heights and new fans. They needed her for the future of the league and Engelbert was afraid to put her foot down in the wake of immense jealousy, hatred and pettiness from her peers.

While the WNBA was drawing record attention, another controversy was brewing: money.

The league had never made a profit. It always operated on a deficit, but players argued that their compensation wasn't keeping pace with the league's rapidly increasing popularity and revenue.

At the 2025 All-Star Game, players wore shirts reading: "Pay Us What You Owe Us."

The message was impossible to miss.

The dispute centered on the league's revenue-sharing structure and the players' belief that they deserved a significantly larger percentage of the money they were helping generate.

The timing was particularly significant.

The WNBA was negotiating a new collective bargaining agreement while simultaneously celebrating record ratings, attendance, sponsorships and media-rights revenue.

Ultimately, the sides came to an agreement, but Clark deserves the credit for that. The deal also raised questions about whether the new CBA was financially responsible. Time will tell.

Then came the moment that arguably did the most damage to Engelbert's reputation among players.

In September 2025, Minnesota Lynx star and WNBPA vice president Napheesa Collier publicly delivered a devastating criticism of league leadership.

Collier accused the WNBA of poor leadership, inadequate accountability and failing to properly address player concerns.

Her most memorable assessment was that the WNBA had "the worst leadership in the world."

She specifically criticized Engelbert over officiating, player safety, compensation and communication.

Collier also described conversations with Engelbert in which she said her concerns weren't taken seriously.

Engelbert disputed some of Collier's characterization of their conversations but ultimately acknowledged that she needed to do better and rebuild trust with the players.

Notably, Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham criticized Engelbert in August, calling her a "delusional leader" and stating the league needs a "bold" commissioner who prioritizes players over self-interest.

You'd be hard pressed to find another commissioner with a worse relationship with players.

Engelbert also became involved in one of the most politically sensitive issues in American sports: male participation in women's athletics.

The WNBA faced growing questions about eligibility rules, biological sex and the participation of transgender athletes.

Engelbert put together a task force that has amounted to absolutely nothing, other than providing a clear indication that she and WNBA leadership are so captured by left-wing politics and ideology that neither Engelbert nor the task force can publicly admit that the W in WNBA stands for women and that the proper definition of the word is adult human females.

Fans have been discriminated against for wearing XX-XY T-shirts; Enes Kanter Freedom was confronted by Natasha Cloud for wearing a shirt defining what a woman is; and teenagers sitting courtside in XX-XY T-shirts were verbally abused by a co-owner of the Seattle Storm. Cunningham has been on the receiving end of hard fouls, relentless booing and more since she said men don’t belong in women’s sports and spaces.

In this moment, the WNBA needs a leader to cool the temperature, but Engelbert has failed time and time again.

The league has historically positioned itself as more than a sports organization, taking strong positions on racial justice, reproductive rights, LGBTQ issues and other divisive, left-wing social causes. That alienates fans and is not a good business model. Engelbert will be remembered for allowing the league to be known as the most politically active and divisive in American pro sports.

The WNBA claims to be a league that welcomes everyone, yet some fans and even players increasingly feel that certain political viewpoints aren’t welcome. That’s a problem for which Engelbert is to blame.

In 2026, debates over fan behavior, political speech, men in women's sports and other controversies have become almost as prominent as the basketball itself.

This season will be remembered largely as being overshadowed by controversies involving race, gender, politics and player relations. You can thank Engelbert for that.

The WNBA needs a competent leader who understands business, wants to unite fans around basketball and, most importantly, embraces and markets Caitlin Clark. I won’t hold out much hope for that, though.

item.title: Mysterious $150M superyacht docks in LA with hidden name and magical connection
item.description: Author J.K. Rowling's $150 million superyacht Samsara is reportedly docked in a Los Angeles marina with its name covered, but locals quickly identified the 290-foot vessel.
item.content:encoded:
A mysterious nine-figure superyacht sailed into a Los Angeles marina with its name concealed, but locals apparently didn't need long to figure out the famous name behind the massive vessel.

The boat, which has been docked in Marina del Rey since Sunday, belongs to "Harry Potter" author J.K. Rowling, according to the California Post.

The Post cited its sources, one of whom called it "the worst kept secret on the Marina."

MASSIVE NEW CRUISE SHIP UNVEILS JAW-DROPPING OUTDOOR THEME PARK IN MIDDLE OF THE OCEAN

The yacht's name was reportedly covered soon after docking, but that did little to keep the vessel's identity under wraps.

The superyacht was spotted by those behind the Instagram account twogirls.oneboat, with several commenters identifying the vessel as Rowling's Samsara, according to the Post.

The Post reported that while Rowling has been confirmed as the owner, the "Harry Potter" author has not been seen publicly.

Pictures show the enormous white superyacht docked in the marina, towering over its surroundings.

BELOVED CRUISE SPOT WILL BE OFF LIMITS THROUGH 2027 AS SAFETY CONCERNS LINGER

Superyacht broker Chris Cecil-Wright told Fox News Digital owners will sometimes take steps to make their vessels less easily identifiable, although he said concealing a yacht's name is "very rare."

"Quite often, you'll find that if a boat is at anchor or in a port you might switch off AIS [Automatic Identification System], so people can't instantly work out where you are," the United Kingdom-based expert said. 

"Very occasionally, if there's a particular event or something going on, you might find an owner might conceal the obvious names on the side of the boat."

Cecil-Wright said privacy itself is a major draw for wealthy and high-profile yacht owners.

"Particularly when you're a recognizable face or name, it becomes increasingly difficult to be able to relax anywhere in public," he said. 

CLEANEST CRUISE LINES REVEALED AFTER CDC SURPRISE SANITATION INSPECTIONS

"So being on a private yacht, which is often sort of looked at as a private island, is the real luxury."

At 290 feet long, the ship is nearly the length of a football field.

The vessel can accommodate 12 guests and a crew of 26, and features a circular swimming pool, cinema and beach club, according to the website SuperYachtFan.

The superyacht was built by Oceanco and delivered in 2015 under the name Infinity.

The yacht is worth an estimated $150 million, according to SuperYachtFan, with an estimated running cost of up to $15 million a year.

The ship's first owner was businessman Eric Smidt, who sold it to Australian billionaire businessman Brett Blundy.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

In 2023, the ship was sold to Rowling, who named the boat Samsara, a Sanskrit word meaning "wandering."

Fox News Digital reached out to Rowling, but she declined to comment. 

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Rowling, who was a single mother receiving government assistance when "Harry Potter" was published, has since become one of Britain's wealthiest authors.

Her net worth stood at a staggering $1.2 billion as of Sept. 4, according to Forbes.

For the ultra-wealthy, superyachts offer a rare combination of luxury and privacy, essentially serving as floating mansions that can travel from one exclusive destination to another.

Earlier this year, Fox News Digital reported that luxury hotel brands were increasingly taking their five-star services to sea, launching intimate superyachts aimed at wealthy travelers who have traditionally avoided crowded cruise ships.

item.title: Tennis star Aryna Sabalenka stops US Open match because of overwhelming marijuana stench
item.description: Aryna Sabalenka stopped her US Open match to complain about weed smoke, telling the umpire the smell was "so strong" during her third-round win.
item.content:encoded:
The US Open is developing a reputation for debauchery, and on Friday, things got so bad that tennis star Aryna Sabalenka stopped a match because, apparently, the stadium smelled more like weed than your neighbor’s van with the Dio album cover airbrushed on the side.

The Belarusian was taking on Uzbekistan's Kamilla Rakhimova in a third-round match Friday in Queens.

However, during the match, she was seen saying something to the crowd and then approached umpire Eva Asderaki‑Moore.

ARYNA SABALENKA FIRES BACK AT REPORTER FOR ASKING QUESTION ABOUT PARTYING AFTER US OPEN VICTORY

"Someone is smoking weed," Sabalenka could be heard saying. "Do you mind? Because it’s so strong."

Sabalenka went on to win the match — despite the threat of a contact high — but it brings the US Open's weed problem under the microscope again.

GROUP OF INFLUENCERS FORCES PAUSE DURING US OPEN MATCH WITH CRINGEWORTHY PHOTOSHOOT IN SUITE

This has been a running thing for a few years now, ever since weed was legalized in New York City. Players have had to battle through the stench of bubonic chronic in the vicinity of some courts.

However, this year, according to The New York Post, local dispensaries are even delivering some sticky icky to tennis fans.

"You get high, it makes [tennis] a little more entertaining," Tre Davidson, a manager at a nearby dispensary, Silk Road, told the outlet.

Wow. Okay. So, weed has the same effect on tennis that it does on Pink Floyd's "Dark Side of the Moon" and Cheech & Chong's entire body of work.

The more you know...

Having a good time is one thing, but when it starts impacting those who do not wish to take part in your puff-puff-passing — namely the athletes — then maybe it's time to put it out.

This will be a tough battle, but the answer is in plain sight: edibles.

Clear out the smoke so that athletes can suck down some of the crisp, clean New York City air during their match.

Meanwhile, fans can still get stoned out of their gourd to make tennis more interesting or to make them wonder what would happen if you crossed a pizza with a Taco Bell Crunchwrap Supreme.

item.title: Charter school network files First Amendment lawsuit after state blocks AP scores from US News
item.description: Success Academy filed a First Amendment lawsuit after Betty Rosa blocked AP exam data from U.S. News rankings, tanking its rank from 11th to 196th.
item.content:encoded:
Success Academy, New York City’s largest charter school network, is pushing back against the New York State Education Department (NYSED) over what it calls a violation of its First Amendment rights.

The charter network filed a federal lawsuit against New York State Education Commissioner Betty A. Rosa, challenging the state’s refusal to authorize the College Board to release Advanced Placement (AP) exam results for New York public schools to U.S. News & World Report for its annual high school rankings.

"There's no question that it's a First Amendment violation because, essentially… a publication right is being prevented from reporting real news," Eric Grannis told Fox News Digital. Grannis is an attorney representing the lawsuit and the husband of Success Academy CEO Eva Moskowitz.

BUSINESS BOOMS FOR FIRM THAT RECRUITS STUDENTS AS ENROLLMENT IN SCHOOL DISTRICTS TANK NATIONWIDE

U.S. News & World Report compiles its nationally recognized high school rankings using academic criteria, including student participation and performance on AP exams.

"Now, it both determines the ranking, and the information is also provided by U.S. News & World Report," Grannis added. "So, you can see how many students participated in AP exams, how many, and how well the students did, and how many exams they took. And this has not been a problem for decades."

"But just this year, Betty Rosa, the commissioner of the New York State Education Department, decided that they would not allow U.S. News & World Report to report on any of these AP grades," he said.

The lawsuit alleges that NYSED’s policy violates the First Amendment by preventing Success Academy from communicating truthful, independently verified information about its students’ academic performance. The network said that U.S. News relies directly on data from the College Board—the organization that administers AP exams—to build its annual school rankings.

Because NYSED declined to authorize the College Board to release 2026 AP scores, U.S. News calculated the advanced course metrics using only International Baccalaureate (IB) data. Because Success Academy offers AP courses rather than IB programs, the network received zero credit for 40% of the ranking's weighted criteria, causing its statewide ranking to crater from 11th to 196th.

"All of this critical information about this incredible success of its students has been suppressed by the New York State Education Department. And so we have brought a First Amendment lawsuit to require the commissioner to allow this data to be made public," Grannis told Fox News Digital.

TRUMP ADMIN TO MAKE HISTORIC INVESTMENT IN CHARTER SCHOOLS AMID NATIONWIDE DECLINE IN PUBLIC SCHOOL ENROLLMENT

Success Academy accused NYSED of obscuring data to artificially inflate the rankings of traditional public schools at the expense of high-performing charter schools. The network noted that while less than 25% of high school graduates nationally pass an AP exam, 95% of Success Academy’s 2026 graduating class passed three or more AP exams, with 60% passing seven or more.

Founded in 2006, Success Academy serves over 22,000 predominantly low-income, Black, and Hispanic students across New York City. The network regularly highlights its academic performance against some of the state's wealthiest suburban districts, such as Scarsdale Union Free School District, where fewer than 10% of students are Black or Hispanic and zero percent are categorized as economically disadvantaged.

According to state test scores released for grades 3-8 in 2025, Success Academy ranked No. 1 in New York State for math proficiency with a 96% pass rate. The network also placed second statewide in English Language Arts (ELA) with a 92% pass rate—trailing Scarsdale by just one percentage point.

NYSED has defended its position by citing student data privacy laws, saying that student information should not be commercialized for ranking products. However, Grannis argued that applying commercial restrictions to educational reporting sets a dangerous precedent. He noted that major news outlets like The New York Times and The Washington Post are also commercial entities, but their for-profit status does not diminish their First Amendment protections.

NATION'S REPORT CARD GIVES PUBLIC SCHOOLS A FAILING GRADE. PARENTS ARE DEMANDING BETTER

"If the commissioner had her way... it would strike at the heart of the First Amendment," Grannis said. "It would mean that in theory, she could prohibit anybody from reporting on, say, the average reading scores of New York City school students because that would be, in her view, profiting—having a newspaper article in a for-profit magazine about student data."

Grannis also alleged that NYSED's decisions are heavily influenced by traditional public school interests and teachers unions.

"The Department of Education is particularly highly aligned with the teachers union," Grannis claimed. "The teachers union is adamantly against accountability. They don't like there to be lots of public information getting out there about how well students are doing because it's going to point out that the students at charter schools are generally doing far better than the students at the district schools that are unionized."

Success Academy has a long history of friction with teachers unions, particularly over sharing space in public school buildings, known as co-locations. Charter schools receive public funding on a per-pupil basis, creating financial competition with traditional district public schools.

The United Federation of Teachers (UFT) filed a lawsuit in 2023 seeking to block two Success Academy co-locations in Brooklyn and Queens, arguing in part that the city failed to account for a state-mandated class-size law.

Grannis argued that the state's move to suppress score releases reflects a broader policy stance against standardized metrics.

"They have made this very public for years... they call it 'less testing, more teaching,'" Grannis said. "I think it might be more accurately titled 'less teaching, less accountability,' because essentially it hides the failure of the district schools to obtain results. And you know what governments do when they don't like unfavorable comparisons: they suppress information."

NYSED did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment.
